newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers move into Arab East Jerusalem houses.
newsitem.headline: Settlers move into Arab East Jerusalem houses.

text.p: Jewish settlers moved overnight into five houses of an Arab East Jerusalem neighbourhood, a spokesman said on Thursday.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office had no immediate comment on an Israel Radio report which quoted a member of parliament as saying the Israeli leader had been informed of the secret move and had given his support.
Yehoshua Mor-Yosef, a spokesman for Israel's National Religious Party which champions Jewish settlement, said the families had legally bought the homes.
"They went in at night in five houses that they acquired recently," he told Reuters. "They entered quietly in the night and got up this morning and it's still quiet."
He denied there was any significance to the timing. Israel faced international condemnation this week for breaking ground on a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem for 6,500 Jewish families.

In 1991 a first group of settlers took over homes in Silwan, home to 30,000 Palestinians, attaching importance to the area in East Jerusalem -- just outside the Old City walls -- where they say the biblical King David built the first capital of the Jewish people.

Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East War, annexed it to the Jewish western sector and views it as part of its "eternal, indivisible" capital. Palestinians regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state and the settlers as a provocation.
